$comment: Page types, domains and mood words used by scripts/compose.mjs. Every id must exist in catalog.json (checked by tests/unit/compose.test.mjs).

pageTypes.name: Product landing page
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands
pageTypes.primary: Under the hero headline, and again in the closing CTA band. Nowhere else.

sections.copy: Brand left, 3–5 links, one CTA right ("Start free").
sections.rule: Use navbar-simple instead when there is only one product area. Its button repeats the hero's action with the same words; any other action in the bar is a text link.

sections.copy: Eyebrow (≤4 words) → headline that says the outcome (≤10 words) → one sentence of how → one CTA + one quiet link → one reassurance line ("No card required"). The headline is the page’s h1.
sections.rule: Show the real product on the right, not an illustration.

sections.copy: "Used by teams at" + 5–6 names.
sections.rule: Only with real customers; skip it rather than invent logos.

sections.copy: 2–3 rows. Each: a heading that states a result, one sentence, 2–3 specific points, a real screenshot or a small live mockup built from catalog parts (stat-strip, data-table, a chart) inside a frame marked data-mock. Never a grey box or stock art.
sections.rule: Alternate image left/right. Never more than three rows.

sections.copy: Three to eight words that name what the picture shows, then the product's real screen large (device-frame, a screenshot, a chart), then three figures a visitor can check.
sections.rule: The page's one dark band. The strongest picture you have; nothing decorative.

sections.copy: 3 numbers people can check, each with a plain label and a source.
sections.rule: No vanity totals; one figure per claim.

sections.copy: 3 quotes with name, role and company; each quote names a concrete result.
sections.rule: Only real quotes you may use, with name, role and company. Without them, show a fact strip people can check (customers, uptime, years) or skip the section. Never invent people.

sections.copy: 3 steps, verb-first headings ("Connect", "Set targets", "Share").
5–7 questions buyers actually ask: price, data, switching, security, cancelling.
Restate the outcome in one line + the same CTA as the hero.
sections.rule: Same label as the hero button.

sections.copy: 3–4 columns of 3–5 links, one line about the company, one legal row.

avoid: A second hero further down
Three equal CTAs
Stock illustrations of people
Feature grids with 9+ icons

pageTypes.name: Pricing page
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands
pageTypes.primary: The recommended tier's button is the only filled one.

sections.copy: Same as the rest of the site.
sections.rule: Its button repeats the hero's action with the same words; any other action in the bar is a text link.

sections.copy: Headline that answers "what will this cost me" + monthly/annual toggle with the saving in plain numbers ("2 months free").
3 tiers. Each: who it is for (one line), price, the 4–6 things that differ, one button. Mark one as recommended.
sections.rule: Never four or more tiers above the fold.

sections.copy: Grouped rows; ticks and short values, not paragraphs.
sections.rule: Sticky header row.

sections.copy: Trials, seats, invoices, cancelling, discounts.
"Still deciding?" + talk to sales as the secondary action.

avoid: Hidden prices ("Contact us" on every tier)
Feature lists that repeat across tiers
Countdown timers

pageTypes.name: Analytics dashboard
pageTypes.layout: App shell: sidebar + scrolling main; KPI row then a two-up chart grid
pageTypes.primary: Top right of the page header ("Export", "New report").

sections.copy: 5–9 sections, icons + labels, current one marked.
Title (what this page answers) + "updated 2 minutes ago" + one action.
Date range, segment, compare. One bar for the whole page.
sections.rule: Cards never repeat these filters.

sections.copy: 2–4 figures, each with a label, a change vs the last period and a sparkline.
sections.rule: The most important figure first.

sections.copy: Each chart title is the takeaway ("Team plan pulled ahead in March"), subtitle is the measure and unit.
sections.rule: The widest story spans both columns. Pick charts from references/chart-selection.md.

sections.copy: Sortable, numbers right-aligned and tabular, one row action menu.

states: loading: skeleton of the same layout
empty: say what will appear and give one action
error: what failed, a retry button, keep the filters
avoid: A filter bar inside every card
Pie charts with 5+ slices
Gauges for everything
Dual-axis charts

pageTypes.name: Settings and account
pageTypes.layout: Settings: section nav + one form column (max 420px)
pageTypes.primary: A sticky save bar that appears only after a change; switches save instantly.

sections.copy: General, Members, Billing, API, Notifications, Danger zone.
Name, URL, time zone. One column, labels above fields.
Switches that apply immediately, each with one line of description.
Invite by email, role per row, remove.
Current plan, next invoice, payment method; usage below it.
Each limit as a meter with used / limit.
Masked key, copy, roll with a second confirm.
Last on the page. Type the name to confirm.
"You have unsaved changes" + Discard + Save. Copy the save bar from the settings blueprint (#savebar); the sticky-action-bar component is a purchase bar.
sections.rule: Only for fields that do not save instantly.

states: saving: button shows progress
error: inline under the field, never only a toast
avoid: Two-column forms
Save buttons at the top
Delete next to Save

pageTypes.name: Documentation
pageTypes.layout: Three columns: tree nav, article at 68ch, "On this page" rail
pageTypes.primary: None in the article; the top bar holds search and one CTA ("Get API key").

sections.copy: Logo, product switcher, ⌘K search, one CTA.
Grouped by task, not by internal module names.
Title = the task ("Send your first event"). Short intro, then numbered steps.
sections.rule: Text never wider than 68ch.

sections.copy: Tabs per language, copy button, real values.
Only for warnings and prerequisites.
sections.rule: Max two per page.

sections.copy: Previous and next, each naming the page it opens.

states: not found: search box plus the 5 most visited pages
avoid: Walls of callouts
Screenshots of code
Marketing copy inside docs

pageTypes.name: Sign in and onboarding
pageTypes.layout: Split: form left (max 400px), product image or quote right; stacks on phones
pageTypes.primary: One full-width button in the form.

sections.copy: Heading says where you are ("Sign in to Halyard"). Email first, SSO as secondary.
6 boxes, paste fills all, resend after 30s.
3–4 steps max, each with one question.
3–5 tasks with progress.

states: error: under the field, keep what was typed
loading: button shows progress, form stays visible
avoid: Password rules revealed only after failing
Captcha before trying
Two primary buttons

pageTypes.name: Directory or catalogue
pageTypes.layout: Search on top, filters left or as chips, card grid that never needs a breakpoint
pageTypes.primary: Search is the main control; each card has one action.

sections.copy: Placeholder names what you can search ("Search 240 integrations").
4–8 chips, counts on each, clear all.
Same card height, name, one-line summary, 1–2 facts.
Show the total.
Say what was searched, offer to clear filters.

states: empty: suggest a broader search
loading: skeleton cards
avoid: Infinite scroll with a footer
Cards of different heights

pageTypes.name: Blog or editorial
pageTypes.layout: Single column at 68ch; images may break out wider
pageTypes.primary: Subscribe, once, after the article.

sections.copy: Name in the middle, sections left, subscribe right.
Headline that says the point, standfirst, byline + date + read time.
3 related pieces with dates.
What arrives and how often ("One email a month").

avoid: Pop-ups before reading
Share bars that follow the text
Body text below 17px

pageTypes.name: Portfolio or studio site
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column; work in a two-up grid
pageTypes.primary: "Get in touch" in the top bar and at the end.

sections.copy: Name, Work, About, Contact.
One sentence about what you make and for whom. The headline is the page’s h1.
sections.rule: Drop the announcement pill and the product mockup: a portfolio hero is the statement and one link.

sections.copy: 4–6 projects as large plates: name, type and place, year. Put a real photo or drawing in each plate; without images every plate keeps the same numbered style.
2–3 short quotes.
sections.rule: Only real quotes you may use, with name, role and company. Without them, show a fact strip people can check (customers, uptime, years) or skip the section. Never invent people.

sections.copy: Email, availability, what to include.

avoid: Skill bars with percentages
Auto-playing showreels with sound

pageTypes.name: Store product page
pageTypes.layout: Split: gallery left (60%), buy box right (40%); buy box sticks on desktop
pageTypes.primary: "Add to bag" in the buy box; on phones a sticky bar repeats it.

sections.copy: Brand centred, categories left, search + bag right.
sections.rule: Its button repeats the hero's action with the same words; any other action in the bar is a text link.

sections.copy: 4–6 photos with thumbnails that switch the main view (the store blueprint’s .sp-gallery), zoom on click.
h1 name, tasting or key facts, price (was/now only if real), options as segmented control and chips, one-off vs subscription as radio cards, delivery date, Add to bag with the total on the button.
Average, count, distribution, 3 recent reviews.
Materials, sizing, delivery and returns.
Price + Add to bag.
sections.rule: Phones only.

sections.copy: 4–8 items, never required to buy.

states: out of stock: say when it is back, offer a notify button
avoid: Fake urgency ("Only 2 left!")
Price hidden until checkout
Pop-up discount on load

pageTypes.name: Checkout
pageTypes.layout: Split: form left (max 560px), order summary right; summary moves on top on phones
pageTypes.primary: One "Pay £X" button whose label includes the total.

sections.copy: Brand only, no navigation, a "Secure checkout" line.
sections.rule: Remove every link that leaves the flow.

sections.copy: Contact → Delivery → Payment.
Email first; postcode lookup; one column.
2–3 options with date and price.
Items, promo code, subtotal, delivery, tax, total.

states: error: under the field and summarised at the top
processing: disable the button, show progress, never double-charge
avoid: Account creation before paying
Surprise fees on the last step

pageTypes.name: Changelog
pageTypes.layout: Single column at 68ch with dates in a left gutter on desktop
pageTypes.primary: Subscribe to updates (RSS or email) in the header.

sections.copy: Date, version, a title that says what changed, 1–3 sentences, an image if visual.
sections.rule: Newest first.

sections.copy: New, Improved, Fixed. One per entry.
"Get one email when we ship something."

avoid: Marketing language for bug fixes
Version numbers without dates

pageTypes.name: Status page
pageTypes.layout: Centred column (max 760px)
pageTypes.primary: Subscribe to updates.

sections.copy: One line: "All systems working" or what is affected, with the time.
sections.rule: Colour plus an icon plus words, never colour alone.

sections.copy: One row per service, 90 days, % uptime.
Past incidents: what broke, impact, fix, times in UTC.
Email or RSS.

states: incident: the banner changes tone and links to the live update
avoid: Green everywhere with no history
Vague "degraded performance" without scope

pageTypes.name: Admin list (users, orders, records)
pageTypes.layout: App shell; page header, one filter row, full-width table
pageTypes.primary: "Invite user" / "New order" top right; bulk actions appear when rows are ticked.

sections.copy: Title + count ("Users · 1,284") + one action.
Search, 2–3 filters, saved views.
Checkbox column, sortable headers, status badges, row menu.
Appears when rows are ticked: count + 2–3 actions.
Rows per page and total.
Opens beside the table so the list stays visible.

states: empty: explain and offer the main action
loading: skeleton rows
error: keep filters, offer retry
avoid: Edit forms in modals for long records
Actions only on hover

pageTypes.name: Desktop work app
pageTypes.layout: Saved views in a sidebar, a calm dense table, an inspector for the selected row; the page never scrolls, panes do. One pane at a time below 860px.
pageTypes.primary: New record top right of the table; the inspector holds the action for the selected row.
states: loading: skeleton rows in the table and the inspector
empty: what this view will hold and the action that fills it
error: what failed, Try again, and the last copy kept
avoid: Modals for editing a record that has an inspector
Actions only on hover
Two tables side by side

pageTypes.name: AI assistant chat
pageTypes.layout: History rail left (a drawer on phones), one reading column for the conversation (max 760px), composer pinned to the bottom
pageTypes.primary: Send, in the composer. Enter sends, Shift+Enter adds a line.

sections.copy: "New chat" on top, then conversations grouped by Today, Yesterday, Earlier, titled by their first question.
sections.rule: On phones it becomes a drawer behind a menu button, never a column of unlabelled icons.

sections.copy: The person's turn in a soft bubble on the right; the assistant's answer as plain prose on the left with its actions (Copy, Retry) underneath.
sections.rule: Answers are text first: headings, lists, tables and code blocks render properly; never one wall of text in a bubble.

sections.copy: A placeholder that says what to ask ("Ask about your revenue…"), attach, model or mode picker only if it matters, Send.
sections.rule: Pinned to the bottom; grows to 6 lines; Stop replaces Send while an answer streams.

sections.copy: One line about what it can do and 3–4 example prompts as buttons that fill the composer.
sections.rule: No mascot, no sparkle icons, no gradient orb.

states: empty: example prompts
streaming: text appears with a caret and a Stop button
error: say what failed under the turn and offer Retry; keep the question
avoid: Purple gradients and sparkle icons to signal AI
Both sides in identical bubbles
Read receipts and typing avatars from messaging apps
A disclaimer longer than the answer

pageTypes.name: Inbox or team chat
pageTypes.layout: Three panes: folders, list, reading pane; collapses to one pane on phones
pageTypes.primary: "New message" top of the list pane.

sections.copy: Resizable list and reading pane.
Sender, subject, snippet, time; unread in bold.
Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line.

states: empty folder: one calm line
offline: banner and queued messages
avoid: Read receipts nobody asked for
Unread badges on every icon

pageTypes.name: 404 and error page
pageTypes.layout: One centred block
pageTypes.primary: "Go to home" or search.

sections.copy: Say what happened, why it might have happened, where to go next.
sections.rule: No jokes at the visitor's expense.

avoid: A wall of links
Animated illustrations that delay the message

pageTypes.name: Contact page
pageTypes.layout: Split: form left, ways to reach you right
pageTypes.primary: Send in the form.

sections.rule: Its button repeats the hero's action with the same words; any other action in the bar is a text link.

sections.copy: Reply time, email, office hours.
Top 4 questions.

states: sent: confirm and say when you will reply
avoid: More than 5 fields
Required phone numbers

pageTypes.name: About and team page
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands
pageTypes.primary: "See open roles" or "Contact us".

sections.rule: Its button repeats the hero's action with the same words; any other action in the bar is a text link.

sections.copy: One sentence of what you do and for whom, as a claim someone could disagree with; skip the mission statement. The headline is the page’s h1.
Two or three short paragraphs: why this exists, what changed along the way, where it is now. Dates and names, not adjectives.
sections.rule: A plain section (class="lt-section" data-layout="rail"): the heading in the rail, the prose beside it at 60 to 72 characters a line. No timeline graphic unless there are at least five real dates.

sections.copy: Three or four figures a reader can check: founded, people, customers, places. Each with its unit and period.
Photograph or initials, name, role. One line on what each person does, if there are fewer than eight.
sections.rule: No photographs? data-variant="list": ruled rows of name, role and one line. Initials on tiles only for a small team with nothing else to show.

sections.copy: Three to five principles as rows: a short name and one sentence that says what you do because of it. Each must rule something out.
sections.rule: Leave out anything every company would say ("We care about quality"). No prices or links in these rows.

sections.copy: Open roles or contact.

avoid: Values written as single words
Stock team photos

pageTypes.name: Developer tool landing page
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands; a floating pill nav over a hero with a grid backdrop
pageTypes.primary: Under the hero headline ("Get an API key" or "Read the docs"), with the install command beside it. Again in the closing band.

sections.copy: Brand, Docs, API, Pricing, Changelog, Sign in, one primary button.
sections.rule: data-variant="pill" floats it over the hero. Docs is always one click away.

sections.copy: Headline: what it does for the code, in under 8 words ("Product events, from one line of code"). Lede: the mechanism and one number. An announcement-pill above for what shipped last.
sections.rule: One primary button and a command-chip with the real install command. data-backdrop="grid spot"; add backdrop-circuit only here.

sections.copy: Three numbered steps beside a terminal that runs the real setup commands and shows their real output.
sections.rule: Six to ten lines. It plays once; never loop it.

sections.copy: The smallest complete example, with tabs for each language you support and a file name.
sections.rule: 8 to 14 lines that would run if pasted. No pseudo-code, no ellipses.

sections.copy: Six things the reader no longer has to build, each a 3–5 word heading and one sentence with a number or a limit.
sections.rule: No adjectives without a figure. Same icon style throughout.

sections.copy: Three real endpoints as rows, the first open with its parameters and a sample response; a link to the full reference.
sections.rule: Method as a word in a tag, path in mono. Skip this section if there is no public API.

sections.copy: Four operational figures with their period: volume, latency, uptime, losses.
sections.rule: Units written out; no rounded vanity numbers.

sections.copy: One engineer, by name and company, saying what they removed or stopped doing, with two or three figures beside it.
sections.rule: One quote, not a wall of logos.

sections.copy: The same action as the hero, plus the free tier and the price after it in one line.
sections.rule: One primary, one ghost link to the docs.

sections.copy: Company, Privacy, Terms, Status, Contact.
sections.rule: Status links to the real status page.

avoid: A dashboard screenshot where code should be
Animated gradient blobs and glowing orbs
Code samples that would not run
Counting GitHub stars as proof when there are few
A second moving background below the hero

pageTypes.name: Agent workspace
pageTypes.layout: Sidebar (workspace switcher, sessions by project, account) and a main pane: a centred start column at rest, a reading column for a running session
pageTypes.primary: Start, in the composer. While a session runs, the one primary is the approval it is waiting for.

sections.copy: The current account and workspace; a grouped menu to change it, with a dot where work is running.
sections.rule: Top of the sidebar. Names, not avatars alone.

sections.copy: "New session" first, then sessions grouped by project, each titled by its task with a state and a time.
sections.rule: State is a shape and a word for screen readers: running, needs you, done, idle. A drawer on phones.

sections.copy: A headline that asks for the task, the composer with a placeholder that names three kinds of input, and a mode switch only if modes differ in what they can change.
sections.rule: Under it, say what the session will use and what it is allowed to do (folder, branch, "asks before it edits").

sections.copy: A quiet dither field behind the start screen only.
sections.rule: Lower its colour until the headline reads on it without a shadow. Never behind a running session.

sections.copy: Three or four recent sessions as rows: title, project, state in words, time.
sections.rule: The whole row is the link.

sections.copy: In a running session: the plan as a checked list, then the change it wants to make.
sections.rule: Nothing is written until the person approves. The approval bar says how many files and stays in view.

states: empty: no sessions yet, with four first tasks that fill the composer
running: plan with one step in progress, the proposed change, an approval bar
error: say which step failed and why; offer Retry from that step
avoid: Sparkle icons, orbs and purple gradients to signal AI
A chat transcript where a plan and a diff would be clearer
Hiding what the agent can touch
Auto-applying changes with no way to stop or review
A loud backdrop behind text people have to read

pageTypes.name: Phone app screen
pageTypes.layout: One 430px column: app bar, content, one primary action in thumb reach, bottom tabs. Stays a centred column on wider screens.
pageTypes.primary: One full-width button above the tab bar. Everything else is a row or a tab.

sections.copy: The screen's name as a large title; back with the previous screen's name on inner screens; at most one text action.
sections.rule: The large title collapses into the bar on scroll. 44px targets.

sections.copy: The one number the person opened the app for, a comparison in words, and a small 7-day view.
sections.rule: One figure, not a dashboard. Tabular numbers.

sections.copy: Two short lists with headings: what needs attention first, then recent history. Name and amount on the first line, detail and status on the second.
sections.rule: Whole-row targets at least 56px tall. Status is a word in a badge, not a colour alone.

sections.copy: Three to five destinations with an icon and a label each.
sections.rule: Labels always visible. A count only where something needs attention.

sections.copy: The primary action opens a sheet with the fewest fields that can work: amount, who, when, send.
sections.rule: Right keyboard for each field (inputmode). Errors in words under the field. Cancel always visible.

states: loading: skeleton of the figure and five rows
empty: one sentence and the primary action
error: what failed and a Retry button, keeping anything typed
avoid: A hamburger menu hiding the main destinations
Icon-only tabs
Desktop tables squeezed onto a phone
Targets under 44px
More than one filled button on a screen
Stretching the layout full width on a tablet

pageTypes.name: Phone app (the whole flow)
pageTypes.layout: Every screen a phone of its own, side by side on a desktop and one at a time on a phone: welcome, the first useful screen, one record, settings. Tab bar, large titles, rows, a sheet for the one form.
pageTypes.primary: One full-width button above the tab bar on each screen. Everything else is a row or a tab.

sections.role: First useful screen: the list and the one action
The one form, in a sheet

states: loading: skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: one sentence in the product's words and the action that fills it
error: what failed and Try again, keeping anything typed
avoid: A tour before the first useful screen
A hamburger menu hiding the main destinations
Icon-only tabs
Targets under 44px
More than one filled button on a screen

pageTypes.layout: A phone first: the balance large, the week of spending as one-hue bars, payments by day, a send sheet with a number pad, the card with a freeze switch; a sidebar and two panes from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Send in the sheet with the amount on the button; everything else is a row or a tab.
screens: A drawing, one sentence, Open an account.
The balance, Send and Card, the week as bars, payments by day.
Its mark, the amount large, the facts as rows.
The card as an object, Freeze, limits, replace.
states: loading: a skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: Pie charts of spending
More than one figure set large on a screen
A colour per category

pageTypes.name: Fitness app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: today as rings with the numbers beside them, the week as bars, a dark workout screen with a huge timer and one action, history by week; a sidebar and two panes from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Start, low on Today; Pause, huge, on the workout.
screens: A drawing, one sentence, Set my goals.
Rings and their numbers, the week as bars, the streak, workouts to pick up, Start low.
The timer huge, intervals as bars, three figures, Pause.
The month as one figure, workouts by week.
states: loading: a skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: A leaderboard of strangers
Badges and confetti
Three charts on one screen

pageTypes.name: Booking app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: who and what, a calm strip of days, a grid of free times, a sheet that repeats the choices beside Confirm, bookings with the next one large; a sidebar and two panes from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Book, low, with the time on the button; Confirm in the sheet.
screens: Who, what, the day, the time, Book low.
The next one as the one card, later, before.
The time large, the facts, move, add to calendar, cancel.
The people or animals it is for, and grouped settings.
states: loading: a skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: A month calendar on a phone
Full times that can be tapped
Asking for an account before the time is chosen

pageTypes.name: Messaging app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: chats with unread counts, a thread with grouped bubbles, day separators, photos, voice notes and the read state, a composer above the keyboard; the list and the thread side by side from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Send, in the composer, lit only when there is text.
screens: Search, rows with the last line, the time and unread counts.
Grouped bubbles, day separators, a photo, a voice note, read state, composer.
states: loading: a skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: Avatars of strangers' faces
A Send button lit with nothing typed
The keyboard covering the field

pageTypes.name: Listening app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: a library with the episode to carry on with, shows as a rail of covers, latest episodes with play; an episode with chapters; now playing rising from a mini player above the tabs; Up next to reorder; a sidebar from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Play, on the card to carry on with and on the player.
screens: A drawing, one sentence, Find shows to follow.
Carry on, shows you follow, latest episodes.
Cover, title, Play from where you were, chapters.
Scrubber with chapters, skip, speed, sleep.

empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again

A scrubber too thin to grab
The player covering the tabs with no way back

pageTypes.name: Ordering app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: the menu as pictures with prices under section chips, an item sheet with its options and the price on Add, a basket above the tabs with the collection time and one Pay, and the order live from received to ready; the basket beside the menu from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Add for £x in the item sheet, then Pay £x in the basket.
screens: A drawing, one sentence, See the menu.
Section chips, items as pictures with prices, the basket bar.
Lines with − and +, when to collect, Pay.
The order on its way, earlier orders with Again.
Ready time, the steps filling, the number for the counter.

empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: A price that changes after Add
The basket hidden behind a tab
Stock photographs of someone else's food

pageTypes.name: Settings-heavy app (phone)
pageTypes.layout: A phone first: who you are, a search that filters every setting, groups of rows that are switches or links with their value, a detail page, closing the account on its own page; a sidebar and two panes from 768px.
pageTypes.primary: Switches act at once; there is no Save. One destructive action, alone, on its own page.
screens: A drawing, one sentence, Get started.
The main list of what the app keeps.
Who you are, search, grouped rows, Close account.
What happens, a typed word, one red button.
states: loading: a skeleton of the figure and the rows on the first useful screen
empty: a drawing of the subject, one sentence in its words and the action that fills it
error: what failed in plain words and Try again
avoid: A Save button for switches
A destructive action among ordinary rows
Settings that only match by label in search

pageTypes.name: Place or venue
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands. Type and art panels carry it until there are photographs.
pageTypes.primary: The booking or visiting action ("Book a table", "Book a tour", "Plan your visit"), in the bar, under the headline and in the booking section. The same words each time.

sections.copy: Name, three or four anchors (what is on offer, booking, visit), and the one action.
sections.rule: No Sign in unless there really are accounts. Every link points at a section on this page or a real page.

sections.copy: Headline: what the place is and the one thing that makes it this place ("Coffee roasted forty steps from your cup"). Lede: what you can do here. Under the buttons: days open and the street.
sections.rule: Right side: a photograph of the place, or an art-panel with its name and one fact until there is one. Never a dashboard frame, never a drawing.

sections.copy: Two to four things (dishes, products, rooms, tours, treatments), each with one line, two facts that differ and the price.
sections.rule: Prices in full. Links named after the thing.

sections.copy: A heading that says what is being booked, four facts beside it (how long, how much, when, how many), then date, time, people and one button.
sections.rule: The answer comes back as a sentence. If booking happens elsewhere, link there instead and say where.

sections.copy: Full address, how to get there by each means with a time, phone and email, and opening hours for all seven days.
sections.rule: Closed days are listed as Closed. Today is marked; "open now" is said in words.

sections.copy: One real review with the person's name and where it was published, and two facts beside it.
sections.rule: Leave this out unless the user gave you a real review. Never write one.

sections.copy: Four to six real questions: booking, access, children, dogs, parking, dietary needs.
sections.rule: Answers in one or two sentences, with the fact first.

sections.copy: Legal name, the same contact links, and one line that is true of the place.
sections.rule: No newsletter box unless they send one.

avoid: Software sections: logo walls, feature grids, "Start free"
A stock photo that is not this place
A hand-drawn illustration of the product or building
An embedded map that loads before the address is readable
Opening hours as an image
Invented reviews, awards or visitor numbers

pageTypes.name: Product brand landing page
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands; the products carry the page
pageTypes.primary: The buying action ("Shop the set", "Buy the starter kit"), with the price beside it, under the headline and in the closing band.

sections.copy: Name, the range, how it works or what is inside, questions, and the buying action.
sections.rule: No Sign in unless there are accounts. Links point at sections on this page.

sections.copy: Headline: what the product does for the person, in their words. Lede: what it is, in one plain sentence with what is in the box. Under the buttons: delivery and returns facts.
sections.rule: Right side: a photograph of the product, or an art-panel with its name, one fact and a flat motif of the subject until there is one. Never a detailed drawing of the product in place of its photograph.

sections.copy: Each product with one line, two or three facts that help choose (size, key ingredient or material, how long it lasts) and its price.
sections.rule: Two to four cards: four sit four across (two by two on smaller screens), so no card is left alone on a row. Vary the art panel tone across the set. Five or more pieces: gallery-rail instead, one ratio, a caption of name and price.

sections.copy: Three numbered steps with a verb first and a time or an amount in each.
sections.rule: Skip it if the product needs no explaining.

sections.copy: Ingredients, materials or specifications as plain label and value pairs, with what each one is for.
sections.rule: Real values only. If you do not have them, leave the section out and tell the user what is missing.

sections.copy: The real average, the real count and two or three real reviews with names.
sections.rule: Leave this out unless the user gave you real reviews. Never write one.

sections.copy: What is in the box, who it suits, delivery cost and time, returns.
sections.rule: Fact first, one or two sentences.

sections.copy: The full offer in one line with the price, and the same button as the hero.
sections.rule: One primary. The button leads to a real basket or checkout.

sections.copy: Shop, Help (delivery, returns, contact), Company.
sections.rule: Legal name and where it is made, if that is true.

avoid: Software sections: logo walls, dashboards, "Start free"
A drawing of the product in place of a photograph
Invented reviews, ratings, percentages or awards
Claims about health or results with no source
A buy button that goes nowhere
Status colours used as decoration on ingredient lists

pageTypes.name: Local or professional service
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column with full-width bands; services and fees as ruled rows, not cards
pageTypes.primary: The booking or contact action ("Book a check-up", "Book a free call", "Get a quote"), in the bar beside the phone number, under the headline and in the closing band. The same words each time.

sections.copy: Name, three or four anchors (what you do and fees, first visit, people, find us), the phone number as text and the one action.
sections.rule: The phone number is a tel: link. No Sign in unless there is a patient or client portal.

sections.copy: Headline: what you do, for whom, and the one thing that sets you apart, in the client's words ("A dentist who tells you the price before the drill"). Lede: who is here, where, and whether you are taking new clients. Under the buttons: what to do if it is urgent.
sections.rule: Right side: a photograph of the real place or the real people, or an art-panel that states one concrete fact large (the address, "20 minutes, free", the call-out fee) until there is one. Nothing worth stating? Use hero-statement instead. Never stock smiles, never a dashboard frame.

sections.copy: One sentence of 12 to 25 words that says how you work differently, as a claim a competitor could not copy, with its second half in data-part="quiet". A mono line of facts under it.
sections.rule: One per page. Leave it out if you cannot write a claim that is true and specific.

sections.copy:
Up to six services as tiles in a plain section: a small label (how long it takes), the service's name, at most one short line, and the price set large at the foot of the tile (

£68

). The main service gets the wide tile in the accent tone. A note under the grid with the date the prices apply from and a link to the full fee list.
sections.rule: Prices in full where they are fixed. More than six services, or prices people compare line by line: service-list rows instead, one short line each. Never "Contact us for pricing" on every tile.

sections.copy: Three steps from first contact to a plan in writing, each a card with a number, a title of three to six words, one line, and a picture: a figure set large ("10 minutes"), the screen the client sees, or the document they take home (invoice-sheet as a written plan or quote).
sections.rule: Written for someone anxious or busy. Every card has a picture; no card is only words.

sections.copy: Each person: name, role, the qualification or registration that matters to this client, and what they mostly do. With four people or fewer the block sets each as a row with room for a line about them: write that line.
sections.rule: Real names and real registration bodies only. Photographs of the real people; without them, four or fewer people already sit as rows with initials, and more than four use data-variant="list".

sections.copy: One real client with a name (or a role, with permission), saying what changed for them.
sections.rule: Leave this out unless the user gave you a real quote. Never write one.

sections.copy: Address, how to get here by bus, car and on foot, access, phone and email, and opening hours with what to do out of hours.
sections.rule: Opening hours as text in a table, never an image. The block sets "Open now, until 18:00" large by itself: keep data-lt="visit-info". As the page's one dark band (data-tone="dark") it marks the change from what you do to how to come. A service with no premises uses contact-section and says which areas it covers.

sections.copy: The four things people ask before they call: are you taking new clients, what does the first visit cost, can I spread the cost, what if I cancel.
sections.rule: Fact first, one or two sentences.

sections.copy: The first step and its price or length in one line, the booking button and the phone number.
sections.rule: One primary. The phone number is the secondary action. No booking system? The button is a mailto: or tel: link and says so ("Email to book", "Call to book"): never a form that goes nowhere.

sections.copy: Legal name, regulator or professional body with registration number, privacy, complaints.
sections.rule: Regulated professions must name their regulator. Do not invent a number.

avoid: Software sections: logo walls, feature grids, "Start free"
Stock photographs of smiling models
"Contact us for pricing" where a price could be given
Invented reviews, star ratings, awards or registration numbers
Claims about results or cures with no source
A contact form as the only way to reach a person

pageTypes.name: Charity or community group
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column divided by hairlines; the claim in type, figures with sources, one giving action
pageTypes.primary: Two actions, in this order when people come here for help: the help route ("Get food this week") is the first button in the hero and the first section; the giving action ("Donate") is in the bar and the closing band. For a charity that does not serve people directly, Donate is the hero's button.

sections.copy: Name, anchors for getting help, where the money goes and ways to help, and Donate.
sections.rule: Getting help comes before giving in the link order.

sections.copy: Headline: what you do and for how many, as a plain fact ("Food for 410 households a week, from one church hall"). Lede: how, in one sentence. Three figures: people helped, who does the work, the share of each pound that reaches the cause.
sections.rule: Every figure is real and has a period ("a week", "in 2025"). No photographs of people in distress. If people in need are an audience, their button comes first and is the filled one; Donate is the second.

sections.copy: Where to come, what to expect in three plain lines (no referral, you choose, we can deliver), a phone number, and the session times.
sections.rule: Leave this out if the organisation does not serve people directly. Never ask for proof of need on the page.

sections.copy: One bar that adds up to a pound, split into two to four parts, each named and explained in a sentence with its total for the year. Link the accounts.
sections.rule: Figures from the latest accounts, with the year. Use a segmented bar and a <dl> in a plain section (class="lt-section" data-layout="rail"); the cause blueprint has one. Leave it out if there are no accounts yet.

sections.copy: Three or four ways to help as tiles in a plain section: a label, a title of a few words, its one link, and a figure where there is one ("£5" a month, "3 hrs" a week). The money tile is wide and in the accent tone.
sections.rule: Each row links to a real page or form.

sections.role: Someone it helped, or who helps
sections.copy: One real person, with their permission, in their own words.
sections.rule: Leave this out unless the user gave you a real quote and consent. Never write one.

sections.copy: Do I need a referral, can I claim tax relief on a gift, is it safe, what do you not accept.
sections.rule: Fact first, one or two sentences.

sections.copy: What one concrete amount does ("£12 fills one household's gap for a week"), then Donate and Give monthly.
sections.rule: A real, checkable equivalence. No urgency tricks, no countdowns.

sections.copy: Legal name, registered charity number, privacy, safeguarding, accounts.
sections.rule: Do not invent a registration number: ask for it.

avoid: Photographs of people in distress, or stock photographs of anyone
Guilt, urgency timers, pre-ticked monthly gifts
Invented figures, stories, quotes or partner logos
A donate button that opens a third-party page with no warning
Software sections: feature grids, pricing tiers, "Start free"
Decoration in place of the facts: where, when, how much reaches the cause

pageTypes.name: Event or conference
pageTypes.layout: Centred page column divided by hairlines; the date and place in type, the programme as timed rows
pageTypes.primary: The ticket or sign-up action with its price ("Get a ticket · £240"), in the bar, under the headline and in the tickets section.

sections.copy: Name, anchors for programme, speakers, tickets and venue, and the ticket action.
sections.rule: No Sign in.

sections.copy: Above the headline: the date and the place, in full. Headline: what the event is about, as a claim. Lede: how many talks or sessions, from whom, for whom. Three figures: sessions, workshops, places (and how many are left).
sections.rule: The date is a <time> element. If places are limited, give the real number.

sections.copy: Timed rows: start time, title, one sentence with the speaker's name, the room. A small label above each day; a one-day event has one list and no label for a second day.
sections.rule: Times in one format with the time zone stated once. Breaks and lunch are rows too. Link each session to its page if it has one.

sections.copy: Name, role and organisation, and the talk each gives, for six to twelve people; a link to everyone.
sections.rule: Real people who have confirmed. Without photographs use data-variant="list": ruled rows of name, role and talk, never initials on tiles.

sections.copy: One to three tickets: who each is for, the price with tax, and three or four things it includes. The refund rule in the lede. One or two tickets sit centred; do not invent a third to fill a row.
sections.rule: A badge only for a real fact ("108 left", "Sold out"). No fake scarcity.

sections.copy: Address, how to get here by train and car, access, door times for each day, and where to stay.
sections.rule: Leave out the open-now line (no data-lt) when the times are for specific dates.

sections.copy: Refunds, paying by invoice, recordings, food and allergies, the code of conduct.
sections.rule: Fact first, one or two sentences.

sections.copy: Organiser's legal name, code of conduct, accessibility, privacy.
sections.rule: Link the code of conduct.

avoid: A countdown timer
"Speakers to be announced" as a section: leave it out until there are names
Sponsor logos nobody agreed to
Invented attendee numbers or quotes from last year
A schedule as an image or a PDF only
Fake scarcity on tickets

domains.typeWhy: a contract-like serif: measured and formal, and easy to read at length
stencilled site lettering, the kind read at a distance on hoardings, vans and plant
stamped letters, like a van’s signwriting or a rubber-stamped invoice: sturdy and plain
a light-ground pairing with a mono for code, like the tool’s own surface
letters that stay distinct for readers with low vision, or anyone anxious and in a hurry
condensed stadium figures, so dates, times and prices read at a glance
the lettering of station and road signs, built to be read in passing
single-storey a and g, like the letters children learn to write
the lettering of station and road signs, built to be read in passing

notes: Keep every piece of content, every link and every form field. Change how it looks, not what it says.
Add lumina.css and lumina.js (or the tokens) and the <html> data attributes from the install output; delete the old colours, gradients and shadows instead of overriding them.
Map each existing section onto the closest block below and copy its words in. Sections with no match keep their markup and get .lt-band and .lt-container.
One primary button per screen: keep every action, but make the others secondary or ghost.
Replace emoji used as icons with inline SVG icons; replace purple or rainbow gradients with a flat surface.
Every link must go somewhere: point in-page links (#pricing) at real ids, or turn them into plain text.
Run the audit on the old page first, then on yours, and say how the score changed.

directions.$comment: Three distinct looks per domain, used by scripts/directions.mjs and the composer's questions. First = the expected one.
